Would you wander Marrakech alone?  One thing I was honestly nervous about before coming to Marrakech for the first time was safety, especially as a woman travelling alone. Social media can make the medina look super intimidating, chaotic, and overwhelming, but my experience has actually been really positive. Of course you need to stay aware like in any big city, but I’ve spent hours wandering the souks, getting lost in little alleyways, shopping, stopping for mint tea, and exploring on my own and I genuinely felt okay. One thing that helped SO much this time was not carrying all my luggage around with me 😅 dragging a huge backpack through crowded streets instantly makes you feel more stressed and overwhelmed. I used @bounce luggage storage so I could explore Marrakech freely for the day before my riad check-in, and it made such a difference. I could actually enjoy the medina instead of worrying about my bags the entire time. Bounce has thousands of locations worldwide and is a super reliable resource if you find yourself in a similar situation as me. If you’re travelling soon, you can use my code SARAHBOUNCE for a discount! #travelhacks #travelreccommendations #solotraveller

If you’re only staying in Marrakesh, you’re missing half of Morocco. We booked a 3-day Imperial Cities tour and honestly, it changed the whole trip. Day one started in Casablanca at the Hassan II Mosque! one of the largest mosques in the world and the only one in Morocco open to non-Muslims. What makes it even more special? Every Moroccan citizen contributed just $2 toward building it. It sits right on the Atlantic Ocean and the architecture is genuinely breathtaking. From there we drove to Rabat, Morocco’s capital city, which most tourists completely skip. We walked through the Portuguese and Jewish historic neighbourhoods, visited the beaches and soaked in centuries of history. Our guide arranged everything! we even had free time to explore and shop. We ended the day arriving in Fez, checked into our Riad and sat down for dinner. Accommodation, breakfast and dinner all pre-arranged. Genuinely stress free. Day two was a full five-hour guided tour through the Fez Medina, the oldest medieval city in the world, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with over 9,000 streets. We visited a traditional tannery where leather has been dyed the same way for over 1,000 years, met master craftsmen and had the chance to commission custom furniture, carpets and ceramics. Moroccan craftsmanship is on another level. We also visited al-Qarawiyyin — the first university ever founded in the world, built in 859 CE by Fatima al-Fihri, a Muslim woman who used her inheritance to create something that has outlasted empires. We ended in Chefchaouen — the famous blue city nestled in the Rif Mountains. Dinner at the Riad, breakfast arranged in the morning, and then the whole day was ours to explore freely. No guide, just a curated list of must-see spots and good vibes. Marrakesh is beautiful. But Morocco is so much more than one city. @GetYourGuide #MoroccoTravel #MoroccoItinerary #MoroccoTravelGuide #VisitMorocco #ImperialCitiesMorocco​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

The film criticizes the historical policy of Arabization in Moroccan education, which marginalized Amazigh language and culture. Its central idea is that a language is more than a way of communicating: it carries a people's identity, history and culture. When children are forbidden from learning in their mother tongue, they can feel that their own identity is being treated as inferior. Abdellah, the teacher, isn't simply fighting to keep teaching in Tamazight. He's defending the children's right to learn in a language they understand and the right of Amazigh people to preserve their identity.. #Razzia #amazigh #edit #fyp #morocco

Imagine what North Africa looked like over 100,000 years ago! This reconstruction is associated with the remains of a child discovered at Contrebandiers Cave near Témara, Morocco, dating to around 108,000–115,000 years ago. Research on the fossil confirms that the child had facial anatomy consistent with Homo sapiens. It is fascinating because North Africa’s ancient human history is far more complex than modern racial categories suggest. The Sahara has undergone dramatic climatic changes, including periods when parts of it were much greener and wetter, allowing human populations to inhabit and move through regions that are now arid. The wider fossil record, including the approximately 315,000-year-old remains from Jebel Irhoud in Morocco, also demonstrates the importance of North Africa in the story of human origins. But let’s be clear: a facial reconstruction cannot establish someone’s modern racial identity, and one ancient individual cannot represent every population that lived in North Africa. Nor does this mean that Amazigh people who look different from this reconstruction are any less indigenous to North Africa. The region’s history involves deep ancestry, population movements and, at different periods, admixture between populations. We don’t need to turn archaeology into a competition over who is or isn’t African. We can acknowledge the evidence, appreciate the complexity of our shared human history and learn from it without trying to force the past into modern racial categories. 🇲🇦🌍 #africanhistory #africantiktok  #prehistoric #historytok #morocco
